title: GraphQL in one idea

kcs.statement: GraphQL exposes a single endpoint where the client specifies exactly which fields it needs, avoiding the over-fetching and multiple round trips of several REST calls, at the cost of harder HTTP caching and query-cost control.

problem_ideas: A mobile profile screen needs 3 REST calls returning 40 fields but shows 6; how would GraphQL change this?
Why can a CDN cache GET /products/9 easily but not a GraphQL POST query?
A client sends a deeply nested query that hits the database 10,000 times; name a defence.
Choose REST or GraphQL for a public payments API and for a dashboard with many widgets.
Count round trips over a 150 ms link for 3 sequential REST calls vs 1 GraphQL query.
Write the GraphQL query for a user's name and their last 5 post titles.
